newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Land Securities plans on target.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Land Securities plans on target.

text.p: British property giant Land Securities Plc said on Wednesday its development plans were on target, with many of them already largely pre-let.
"Yes, they (the developments) are on target, although you can never be totally sure," Land Securities chairman Sir Peter Hunt told Reuters in an interview.

Hunt said that while there was a feeling there was more rental growth to come, so far it had been patchy. Growth in rental rates would be slower than in the 1980s and because it was not across the board it was crucial to be selective in the properties and developments chosen.

Earlier Land Securities reported pre-tax profits of 128.9 million stg for the first half of the year. This included the sale of investment properties and represented an increase on the 118.1 million stg figure for the same period in 1995.

Land Securities' finance director Jim Murray told Reuters a drop in revenue profit for the half year, to 115.5 million stg from 118.2 million stg the previous year, was widely expected and had been flagged in advance.
This reflected the fact that the group was financing a large development programme and was not capitalising interest as part of the cost of carrying this out.
Hunt said property developments continued to be higher yielding business but that most land-owners were holding out on the sale of good land.
"(There is) a much better performance on a development. It is the best growth stock....its very much in demand. That's why we are concentrating on doing as much development as we can," Hunt added.

The group was also buying investments in the "second-hand" market. "We are pursuing both avenues," he said, pointing out that Land Securities had recently added the Team Valley Retail Park, south of Newcastle-upon-Tyne, to its portfolio.
This would make "a substantial and valuable addition to our 500 million stg retail warehouse portfolio," he said in his chairman's statement.
During the half year the company had bought, or agreed to buy, nearly 80 million stg of investment properties.

Hunt said he did not think there would be a less favourable environment for the group if Britiain's opposition Labour party won power from the ruling Conservative government at the next general election, due to be held by May 1997.
"I believe the strategies we are pursuing will apply equally within a "New Labour' environment as in a Conservative (one)."
Restrictions on out-of-town shopping centres, likely to continue whatever the colour of the next government, will not adversely affect the group's activities, he said.
Its existing out-of-town developments would benefit from their position while attempts to enhance city centre shopping and provide better access would benefit its in-town properties.

Hunt said that while he could not comment on possible acquisition targets, the firm looked at "everything from time to time" but would have to "want to own quite a high proportion of the properties" of any target company before making a bid.
